thread:
jas: hey team, day 1 question. I set up a hosted API key but streaming tests randomly return 429 rate_limit_exceeded. Is hosted on the same limits as sandbox?
help-bot: welcome Jas! :wave: Sandbox = low dev quotas. Hosted keys use org quotas and are higher, but still enforce per-request, per-token and concurrency limits.
jas: ah ok. any quick client-side fixes?
ryan: yes — honor Retry-After when present, otherwise exponential backoff + jitter. for streaming, try lowering max_tokens or reduce concurrent streams.
maya: embeddings note: sandbox concurrency is small; batching helps but keep per-request vectors < 256 in sandbox. hosted can take larger batches but watch total concurrent requests.
jas: how do I check my quota as a new hire? I don't see metrics.
help-bot: file an infra ticket at https://redwood.internal/it-requests with subject "map user for quota" and include your github email. infra maps you and then Console metrics appear.
jas: if I need a temporary sandbox bump for a demo, who handles that?
ryan: use the onboarding form pinned in #new-hires, include dates and expected volume. small bumps usually done within 12 hours.
jas: thanks — saved. one more: should my client auto-fallback to a smaller model on 429s?
maya: yes, fallback to a compatible quantized or smaller variant and add a circuit-breaker after repeated 429s to avoid thrash.
jas: perfect, thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
